items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Foozie Rye; the mention comes solely from the interviewer: 'Foozie Rye's about the only one I know around that knows it today.'

ctx.x: Oh man, the piano player had a big chord in front, you couldn't think that quick, you know, like waltzes would be like an A flat or B flat or B flat or A flat, when it was, you go right into a waltz, see, usually, Let Me Call Your Sweetheart or Girl Of My Dreams or, there wasn't too much of a right to waltzes. We would play, you know, just one every fourth piece would play, and the band would take a rest, see, and then the piano player would play, and then, see, on the other tune, played, this tune goes shocked,…

Did you ever play underneath Hawaiian skies? You know that, uh... Foozie Rye's about the only one I know around that knows it today. If I hear it, what? Raymond knows it. If she'd turn the machine off, I'd try to sing it. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
The women there, there were a bunch of characters, they said the Broken Dishes there. The Broken Dishes? That was her name. I had Fazola's applause with Bebe.
